title: Rosalind and the Inheritance
premise: True-crime podcaster Coral Joubert arrives in the fog-bound town of Rosalind to investigate the 1912 disappearance of a witness to the founder's death—only for the town council's ceremonial exhumation of that founder, Ambrose Vane, to reveal an empty coffin. As Coral digs into the case, he discovers the 'dead' witness, Elsie March, may have lived on under another name inside Rosalind itself, protected by families who built their fortunes on her silence. When Coral's informants begin dying and his own past in the town surfaces through a mother he never knew, he realizes the empty coffin was a message meant to flush out anyone who still remembered. In the end, Coral finds Elsie's granddaughter guarding the truth: Ambrose faked his death and fled, and the town's founding legend is a lie. Exposing it costs Coral his anonymity and nearly his life, but gives him the belonging he never had—and a choice between love and duty he finally refuses to make alone.
about_author: K. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing small-town records before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about places that keep their secrets politely.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case
chapters.summary: Coral Joubert, POV: driving into Rosalind with a box of 1912 case files, narrating his podcast intro about the vanished witness Elsie March. He wants a season finale, not roots. Emotional beat: restless ambition masking loneliness; the town already feels uncomfortably like somewhere he's been.

chapters.title: A Town That Smiles Back
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: checks into the Bellwether Inn, interviews the cheery mayor and the hostile historical society president, Marla Vane. Everyone is charming; everyone deflects. A waitress slips him a note: 'Ask about the coffin.' Emotional beat: unease beneath hospitality—the town is performing itself for him.

chapters.title: Exhumation Day
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: the town gathers as Ambrose Vane's coffin is raised for its centennial reinterment ceremony. The lid opens on empty air. Screams, cameras, silence. Coral records everything while Marla stares at him like she expected this. Emotional beat: shock curdling into exhilaration—the story just became his.

chapters.title: What the Ground Keeps
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: police seal the cemetery; Coral pulls century-old sexton logs showing the coffin weighed almost nothing at burial. First hint Ambrose never lay there. A threatening voicemail arrives from an unknown number. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by the first real fear.

chapters.title: Elsie March, Deceased
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Coral at the county archive; brief interlude of an unnamed old woman listening to Coral's podcast in a shuttered house. Her hand trembles over a photograph. Emotional beat: dramatic irony—the witness everyone mourns is breathing, and Coral doesn't know it yet.

chapters.title: The Vane Version
chapters.summary: Marla Vane, POV: invites Coral to Vane House, feeds him the official history—Ambrose the saint, Elsie the unstable servant who drowned herself. Coral notices a portrait with a freshly repainted background. Emotional beat: seduction and menace braided together; Marla knows more than she says.

chapters.title: Static on the Recording
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: reviews his exhumation audio and hears a second voice under the crowd—a woman humming a lullaby matching one in Elsie's letters. His innkeeper, Ruth, goes pale when he plays it. Emotional beat: obsession tightening; the case starts answering back.

chapters.title: Ruth's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV: reluctantly tells Coral her grandmother served alongside Elsie and swore Elsie never left Rosalind. She begs him to drop it—two people who asked questions in 1979 died in a boating accident. Emotional beat: fear inherited like furniture; kindness offered anyway.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: reconstructs Ambrose's final year—debts, a mistress, a forged will. If Ambrose ran, someone powerful helped him vanish and needed Elsie silenced or hidden. Coral airs a teaser episode. Downloads explode; so do the threats. Emotional beat: momentum versus mounting danger.

chapters.title: Someone in the Gallery
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: someone ransacks his room, taking only the 1912 letters, leaving cash—an apology or a bribe. He chases a figure through the fog and loses them at the old cannery. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo; invisibility, his lifelong armor, is failing.

chapters.title: Blood in the Bellwether
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dane Okafor, POV: the archive clerk who helped Coral is found dead, staged as a fall. Dane suspects Coral brought this storm with him but shares an old unsolved file anyway. Emotional beat: grief and wary alliance; the town's politeness cracks open.

chapters.title: The Mother Question
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: Ruth, shaken by the death, admits Coral's birth mother was a Rosalind girl sent away in the nineties—his instinct that the town felt familiar wasn't imagination. Emotional beat: identity quake; the mystery outside has become a mystery inside.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: tracks the stolen letters' provenance to a closed convent school where 'Sister Em' taught for fifty years—initials E.M. He finds her grave, dated three years ago, but fresh flowers on it weekly. Emotional beat: hope sharpening into certainty; the dead keep receiving visitors.

chapters.title: Marla's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marla, POV: offers Coral funding, access, and the town's blessing if he reframes the podcast around Ambrose's heroism. She reveals she knows who his mother was. Emotional beat: temptation with teeth; Coral sees exactly what belonging here would cost.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Tapes
chapters.summary: Coral and Dane, POV split: following the flower deliveries, they find a caretaker's cottage at the decommissioned lighthouse holding reel-to-reel tapes—Elsie's voice, alive until recently, dictating the truth: she saw Ambrose board a boat alive, and the town fathers paid her silence. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by headlights in the drive.

chapters.title: What They Burned
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: the cottage burns behind them; they escape with one tape but the caretaker is gone. Marla's faction moves openly now—Coral is framed for arson. Emotional beat: betrayal and isolation; the hunter becomes the headline.

chapters.title: Granddaughter
chapters.summary: New character Nora, POV: Elsie's granddaughter, raised on the secret, listens to the surviving tape and decides the lie has cost too many lives. She contacts Coral through Ruth. Emotional beat: courage passing down a generation; the witness's blood chooses truth.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin Explained
chapters.summary: Nora and Coral, POV alternating: the full account—Ambrose staged his death with the council's help; Elsie, the only witness, was hidden as 'Sister Em,' guarded rather than killed, because killing her risked exposure. The exhumation was triggered by Marla hunting the tapes before centennial. Emotional beat: revelation as relief and rage at once.

chapters.title: Vane House at Night
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: confronts Marla with the tape as she attempts to burn the last originals in Vane House. Dane arrests her deputy; Marla, cornered, reveals Coral's mother was paid to leave to protect him from exactly this. Emotional beat: climax—truth against legacy, fire and confession under one roof.

chapters.title: The Episode
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: releases the finale from a safehouse—Elsie's voice, the forged death, the town's complicity, his own name included without flinching. Rosalind's legend collapses publicly. Emotional beat: exposure as liberation; invisibility surrendered on purpose.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV round-robin: months later, Ambrose's actual remains are returned; a modest stone for Elsie March is raised beside it. Ruth, Dane, and Nora rebuild the town's memory honestly. Coral walks the cemetery as a local, not a stranger. Emotional beat: mourning and repair; memory made communal.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Coral, POV: he declines a network deal to stay in Rosalind, opening a small archive with Nora and recording a new podcast about towns learning to tell the truth. On the cliff above the lighthouse, he finally answers the question of where he's from. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—love chosen over duty to the story, home chosen over the chase.
